couplet-ahead-head.text: WorkspaceBench poetry: a couplet cut before its rhyme word, read where the bench reads it, the newline ending line one. Across the 100 items the J-lens holds the rhyme word in its top 10 at that newline on only 3, and at the final prompt token on 25, while the model itself puts the word first on 86. So the J-lens mostly does not surface the planned rhyme where the oracle lens does; it is the bank the prose lenses are for. Pinned on that newline.
look: Pin the newline ending line one (#16). J-lens: is "led" anywhere in the top 10 at L43 to L59? On this item it is not; on 97 of 100 items it is not.
Step right to the final space token (#20): the out row has " led" at about 50%, so the model has committed; L53 and L59 sometimes catch it here (25 of 100).
O-lens / NLA, once read on this bank: the bench's oracle lens writes line two with the rhyme already at the newline. Compare its prose at #16 to the J-lens bag.
Search "ahead" to see the rhyme cue itself held across the band; search "led" for the planned word.
